questions.q: What is a functional requirement?
options: What the system must do, like "send an OTP at login"
How fast the pages must load for users
The project's total budget in ₹
Which cloud provider the app will run on

questions.q: Which of these is a non-functional requirement?
options: Users can download invoices as PDF files
The dashboard must load within 3 seconds for 500 users
Admins can block a user account
Customers can pay using UPI

questions.q: Why ask "why" a few times when a stakeholder requests a feature?
options: To delay the project in a polite way
To get the request in writing faster
To uncover the real need behind the request
To estimate the development cost directly

questions.q: The sales head asks for "a report with everything in it". What do you do first?
options: Export every database table to one Excel file
Copy the layout of the old system's report
Ask developers which fields are easiest to add
Ask which decisions it must support and who will use it

questions.q: Which elicitation method best captures how accounts clerks really process GST invoices today?
options: Observing or shadowing them at their desks
A company-wide email survey with rating scales
A brainstorming session with senior management
Reading the ERP vendor's product brochure

questions.q: A requirement reads "The system should be user-friendly." What is wrong with it?
options: It is too technical for business users
It is vague and can't be tested
It belongs in the budget section instead
It should be written as a story title

questions.q: Finance and Operations give conflicting rules for refund approval limits. What is your best move?
options: Pick the rule that is simpler for developers to build
Write down both rules and let developers choose one
Bring both together with facts and impact, and have the decision owner decide
Follow the more senior person's rule without discussion

questions.q: Late in UAT, a stakeholder asks for a "small" change to the loan eligibility rule. What do you do?
options: Add it quietly, since the change is small and urgent
Refuse every change once design has been signed off
Ask testers to update their tests without telling the PM
Assess impact on scope, testing and timeline, then use change control

questions.q: What best shows that a requirement is traceable?
options: It links back to a business objective and forward to its test cases
It is highlighted in a unique colour in the document
It was written and approved by a senior manager
It is saved in a shared drive that everyone can open

questions.q: Which of these is a well-formed user story?
options: Build a UPI report page with a sortable table and an export button
As a shopkeeper, I want to see today's UPI receipts so I can close my day
The database stores all UPI transactions in a separate table
UPI module: high priority, 5 story points, assigned to the backend team

questions.q: What are acceptance criteria?
options: The developer's estimate of the effort needed
The list of people who approve the budget
Conditions a story must meet to be accepted as done
The colours and fonts used on the screen

questions.q: What does a business requirements document (BRD) mainly capture?
options: Server, network and hosting setup details
Detailed code structure and class names
The team's salaries and leave plan
Business needs, goals and the scope of the solution

questions.q: The Given–When–Then format is mainly used to:
options: Write acceptance criteria that can be tested
Draw organisation charts for the client
Estimate story points in planning poker
Plan the team's holidays across sprints

questions.q: A story is too big to finish in one sprint. What should you do?
options: Split it by layer into UI, API and database stories
Split it into thinner stories that each deliver user value
Carry it across several sprints exactly as it is
Remove its acceptance criteria to save time

questions.q: A developer says your story "Customer can cancel an order" is unclear. What should you add?
options: A bolder title and a higher priority label on the story card
More story points so the team has extra time to explore
Rules such as time limits, refund method and what happens after dispatch
A note saying the PM will clarify the details later on

questions.q: Which acceptance criterion is best for "Apply GST on the invoice"?
options: Tax on the invoice should always be calculated correctly by the system
The invoice should look exactly like the one in the old billing system
The tax logic must follow whatever the finance team wants at the time
Given a ₹1,000 item at 18%, the invoice shows ₹180 tax and ₹1,180 total

questions.q: When is a detailed use case more useful than a short user story?
options: For complex flows with many alternate paths, like loan disbursal
For a simple colour change on one button
For fixing a spelling mistake on the login page
Whenever the team works in two-week sprints

questions.q: Auditors ask why the system rejects some vendor payments. Your documents only cover the happy path. What do you do?
options: Ask developers to walk the auditors through the source code line by line
Document the business rules and exception flows, confirm with owners, and version them
Tell the auditors the payment rules are confidential to the company
Write the rules from memory in an email and send it the same day

questions.q: What does an "as-is" process map show?
options: How the work will be done after the change
The project timeline and milestones
How the work is done today
The company's reporting structure

questions.q: In a basic flowchart, what does a diamond shape usually mean?
options: The start or end of the process
A printed document
A data store
A decision point

questions.q: In a process diagram, what are swimlanes used to show?
options: Who performs each step
How long each step takes
The cost of each step
Which steps use AI

questions.q: What does a gap analysis compare?
options: Two competitors' prices for the same product
The current state with the desired future state
Planned and actual project spend each month
Old and new team members' skill levels

questions.q: Loan files wait four days at one desk for a single signature. What is this called in process analysis?
options: A swimlane
A KPI
A bottleneck
A use case

questions.q: What is a SIPOC diagram used for?
options: Detailed screen-by-screen design of an app
Root cause analysis of a single defect
Tracking the team's sprint velocity
A one-page view of who feeds a process and who gets its results

questions.q: Vendor onboarding takes 21 days. Most delay is rework from missing GSTIN and bank details. Best first fix?
options: Check required documents at intake with a checklist and automatic validation
Hire more staff for the approval desk to clear the queue
Buy a new ERP module that has a vendor portal
Set a stricter deadline for approvers to act on files

questions.q: Why is the "5 Whys" technique risky if used on its own?
options: It needs special software and a trained facilitator
It can stop at one cause when several are involved
It only works for IT and software problems
It must be run by internal auditors to be valid

questions.q: Before automating a messy manual process, what should a BA usually do first?
options: Automate it exactly as it runs today
Adopt the software vendor's default flow
Simplify and standardise the process
Wait until staff raise complaints about it

questions.q: Which Excel feature quickly summarises sales by region and month?
options: Spell check
Freeze panes
Page layout
Pivot table

questions.q: What is a KPI?
options: A measurable value showing progress towards a goal
A list of every task in the project plan
A type of key used in database tables
A software licence for reporting tools

questions.q: Two reports show different monthly sales totals. What do you check first?
options: Which of the two reports looks cleaner and better formatted
Whether both use the same definitions, filters and date range
Which of the two reports the manager usually prefers
Which of the two reports was created more recently

questions.q: What does a cohort analysis track?
options: Only the top ten customers by revenue each month
Daily server errors and their response codes
A group of users who started in the same period, over time
Competitors' prices across different cities

questions.q: In a data model, one customer can have many orders. This relationship is:
options: One-to-one
Many-to-many
Self-referencing
One-to-many

questions.q: Why is the median sometimes better than the mean for a "typical" order value?
options: A few very large orders don't distort it
It always gives a higher, safer number
It is much easier to calculate in SQL
It includes all orders, unlike the mean

questions.q: Churn rose after a price change, but a new competitor also launched that month. How do you judge the price effect?
options: Assume the price change caused all of the extra churn this month
Compare similar segments with and without the change, controlling for other factors
Ignore the price change, since the competitor explains everything
Survey only loyal long-term customers about the new price

questions.q: A dashboard shows 98% on-time delivery, yet customers keep complaining about delays. Likely issue?
options: Customers tend to complain whatever the real numbers say
The dashboard uses the wrong colour for late orders
The metric's definition hides delays that customers care about
The server stores delivery times in UTC instead of IST

questions.q: Before migrating customer data to a new CRM, what is the most important BA task?
options: Pick a migration date that suits the vendor's schedule
Train all users on the new screens before anything else
Delete old customer records to save storage space
Profile and clean the data, and agree field mapping with owners

questions.q: Who is a stakeholder in a project?
options: Anyone affected by it or able to influence it
Only the person who pays for the project
Only the development and testing team
Only the external customers who use it

questions.q: What is the main purpose of user acceptance testing (UAT)?
options: Developers check that code follows style rules
Business users confirm the solution meets their needs
Testers measure how much load the server can take
Managers approve the remaining project budget

questions.q: In Scrum, who owns and orders the product backlog?
options: Scrum Master
Tech lead
Product Owner
Each developer

questions.q: MoSCoW prioritisation sorts requirements into:
options: Major, Small, Core and Optional items
Manual, Semi-automatic, Coded and Web
Monthly, Seasonal, Current and Weekly work
Must, Should, Could and Won't have

questions.q: A key stakeholder skips every requirements review. What do you do?
options: Meet them briefly one-on-one, learn their concerns, and agree a format that works
Carry on without them and note their absence in the minutes
Complain to their manager that reviews are being ignored
Send them longer and more detailed documents by email

questions.q: On a power–interest grid, how should you handle a high-power, low-interest stakeholder?
options: Manage them closely with daily meetings
Keep them satisfied with short, focused updates
Ignore them until final sign-off
Send them full detailed reports every week

questions.q: At sprint review the client says a feature "isn't what we asked for", though it meets the story. What now?
options: Show the signed-off story and close the matter firmly with the client
Rebuild the feature at once over the weekend to keep the client happy
Find where understanding diverged, agree the change, and improve how stories get confirmed
Explain that the developer misread the story and it will not happen again

questions.q: Two senior stakeholders each say their feature is the top priority. What helps most?
options: Build both in parallel so that nobody is disappointed
Do whichever one was requested first in writing
Let the delivery team vote on which one to build
Score both on agreed value, cost and risk, and decide with the sponsor

questions.q: After go-live, what best shows the BA's requirements work succeeded?
options: The agreed business outcomes improved, like fewer days to settle claims
The requirements document ran to more than a hundred pages
No change requests were raised by anyone after launch
The developers finished the build ahead of the schedule

task.title: Turn a distributor's email into user stories with acceptance criteria
task.brief: Read the email from a client (below). In about 25 minutes, write: (1) 4–6 user stories in the 'As a ..., I want ..., so that ...' form, each with 2–4 clear, testable acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then is welcome); (2) a short list of open questions you would ask the client before development starts; (3) one or two assumptions or risks you see. A good answer covers what the client really needs (not just what they said), uses concrete rules and numbers from the email, spots the missing or conflicting details, and is written so a developer and tester can work from it.
task.material:
From: Ramesh Iyer, Owner, Sri Lakshmi Distributors (FMCG, Hyderabad)
Subject: Ordering app for our retailers

Hi,
We supply about 600 kirana shops. Today salesmen take orders on paper and phone, and we lose orders and make billing mistakes.
What we want:
- Shop owners should place orders themselves on their phone, in Telugu or English.
- They should see our current price and scheme (e.g. buy 10 get 1 free) for each product.
- Every shop has a credit limit. If the order crosses the limit it should not go through. But my senior salesmen should be able to approve it sometimes.
- Payment by UPI on delivery or credit of 15 days.
- Invoice must have GST correctly, our GSTIN and the shop's GSTIN if they have one (many small shops don't).
- I want to see every evening how much was ordered by area and which shops have not ordered in 10 days.
- Salesmen should get a WhatsApp message when a big order comes.
We need this before Diwali.
Thanks, Ramesh
key_points: Stories written from real user roles (shop owner, salesman, owner/admin) with clear value
Credit-limit rule with the salesman override expressed as testable criteria (who can approve, limits, audit)
GST invoice criteria handling shops with and without a GSTIN
Scheme pricing (buy 10 get 1) shown and applied correctly, with a worked example
Owner's evening report by area and the 'no order in 10 days' list
Language support (Telugu/English) and payment options (UPI on delivery, 15-day credit)
Open questions, e.g. what counts as a 'big order', who sets credit limits, how overdue credit is handled
Notes risks or assumptions such as the Diwali deadline, scope for phase 1, and offline or low-network use

rubric.label: Story quality
rubric.guide: 0 = tasks or features, not user stories, 3 = proper stories but some are vague or too big, 5 = right roles, clear value, sensibly sized

rubric.label: Acceptance criteria
rubric.guide: 0 = missing or untestable, 3 = present but generic, 5 = concrete, testable rules using the email's numbers and edge cases

rubric.label: Gaps and questions
rubric.guide: 0 = takes the email at face value, 3 = a few obvious questions, 5 = finds the real gaps, conflicts and risks

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = understandable but messy, 5 = well organised and ready for a developer and tester
